nt interception, dry-run session vacuum.
# dsh-memory-guard
Host memory and session-log guard for DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`).

It exists because a single DSH session log can grow far past the size the Host
can parse at once. A

real case: a 7,913-line session reached **954 MB
decompressed / 177 MB on disk**, of which 98.5% was

duplicated PTC dispatch
payloads, and opening it exhausted the Host heap. This plugin watches for t

hat
before it happens, blocks the worst single calls, and can shrink existing logs
offline.
## What it does

- **Heap monitoring** — samples `process.memoryUsage()` and
`v8.getHeapStatistics()` every 3 s (used

/ limit / ratio / RSS).
- **Session-log accounting** — scans `$DSH_HOME/sessions` every 15 s, repor

ts
total bytes, file count, and the largest sessions.
- **Runtime guard** — synchronously rejects an

y tool call whose arguments are
estimated above `maxToolArgBytes` (default **2 MiB**), with a messag

e telling
the model to chunk the write or generate the file from a script.
- **Persisted-payload ale

rts** — watches `session/event` rows that were already
appended (`tool/call`, `tool/ptc-dispatch*`)

and warns at 8 MiB, escalates at
32 MiB. Session logs warn at 50 MiB / critical at 200 MiB.
- **Offl

ine vacuum** — `/memguard vacuum` previews; `/memguard vacuum <id>
confirm` rewrites a **cold** sess

ion log: oversized argument strings are
replaced with an identical placeholder in PTC start/final pa

irs, a verified
copy is produced, and the original is kept as `.orig-<timestamp>`.
- **Header chip**

— `MEM 42% · 24.6 MB` in the session header, turning yellow /
red when the Host reports warn / crit

ical.
- **`/memguard` command and `memguard` tool** — status report; the tool also
exposes `vacuum-s
can` / `vacuum-apply` for agents.
## Requirements
| Item | Requirement |

| DSH | tested on `0.2.1-rc.2` (desktop and web profiles) |
| Node.js | `>= 22.15` (uses the built-i

n zstd API; DSH bundles a suitable runtime) |
| Platform | developed and verified on Windows; code i
s path-agnostic, Linux/macOS are untested |

## Header chip

The chip is registered in `conversation.session.header.utilities`. It polls the
same-origin endpoint

`/memory-guard/stats` every 5 seconds. Hover it for heap,
RSS, session totals, the largest session,

recent alerts and recent large
payloads.

If the chip does not appear after a DSH upgrade, the Host functionality still
works through `/memgua
rd` and the `memguard` tool.
## Commands
| Command | Description |

| `/memguard` | Heap, session-log top 5, alerts, recent large payloads, current thresholds |
| `/mem

guard vacuum` | Dry-run: list cold sessions eligible for vacuum and the bytes they could save |
| `/
memguard vacuum <session-id> confirm` | Rewrite that cold session log, verify it, keep `.orig-<times
vacuum <session-id> confirm` | Rewrite that cold session log, verify it, keep `.orig-<timestamp>` |

`memguard` tool actions: `status`, `vacuum-scan`, `vacuum-apply` (the last one
requires `confirm: tr
ue` and refuses live sessions).
## Configuration

Edit the `config` block in the installed `cordis.patch.yml` (or the bundle row in
your profile compo
sition), then restart DSH.
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `guardEnabled` | `true` | Set `false` to disable rejection while keeping monitoring |
| `guardExem

ptTools` | `[]` | Tool names that bypass the size guard, e.g. `["write"]` |
| `maxToolArgBytes` | `2

097152` (2 MiB) | Reject tool calls whose arguments estimate above this |
| `noticeToolArgBytes` | `

524288` (512 KiB) | Only record, do not alert |
| `heapWarnRatio` / `heapCriticalRatio` | `0.75` / `

0.90` | Host heap yellow / red |
| `sessionLogWarnBytes` / `sessionLogCriticalBytes` | `50 MiB` / `2

00 MiB` | Per-session log yellow / red |
| `maxEventWarnBytes` / `maxEventCriticalBytes` | `8 MiB` /

`32 MiB` | Already-persisted event yellow / red |
| `vacuumMinBytes` | `10485760` (10 MiB) | Do not

consider smaller logs for vacuum |
| `notifyCooldownMs` | `300000` | Per session + code alert coold

own |
| `sampleIntervalMs` / `scanIntervalMs` | `3000` / `15000` | Heap sampling / session scan inte
| `sampleIntervalMs` / `scanIntervalMs` | `3000` / `15000` | Heap sampling / session scan interval |
## Why the vacuum is conservative

DSH stores a session as **concatenated zstd frames**, and its reader requires the
**first frame to c

ontain exactly the header line**. Writing the whole file as a
single frame makes the session unlista

ble. This tool therefore writes a
header-only first frame followed by ~1 MiB event frames.

For PTC (`run_code`) sub-calls, DSH logs both `tool/ptc-dispatch-start` (with the
full arguments) an

d the matching `tool/ptc-dispatch`. The session-format
validator requires the pair to carry **deep-e

qual `arguments`**, so deleting the
start row corrupts the session. The vacuum replaces oversized ar

gument strings
with the same placeholder on both sides; line count and `seq` numbers are
preserved.
## Known limitations

- **PTC writes before the guard runs.** For `run_code` sub-calls the Host appends
`tool/ptc-dispatch

-start` before `tools/pre-execute` and the guard, so the
first copy of a huge argument can still rea

ch the log. The guard prevents
execution and the second (result-bearing) row; alerts and vacuum cove

r the
rest. This is documented rather than hidden.
- **Live logs are never rewritten.** Only cold se

ssions can be vacuumed.
- **Only the Host heap is visible.** Renderer memory is not accessible from

a
Host plugin.
- **It does not raise the heap limit.** Node/Electron heap flags are set by the
launc

her, not by a plugin.
- **Vacuum is destructive by design.** It removes oversized payloads from the

copy; the original is kept as `.orig-<timestamp>`, and dry-run is the default
in `/memguard vacuum`.
## Privacy

- Reads local session-log file sizes and (for vacuum) the selected cold log.
- No network requests,

no telemetry, no uploads.
- The web UI only calls the same-origin `/memory-guard/*` endpoints.
